decision.question: Review finding #3: the minion built inspect(subject) as a free function, not instance.inspect()/Class.inspect() as literal methods — which is right?
options: Add a real .inspect() method to every object (would mean patching Object.prototype sitewide, or hand-adding it to every class)
Keep the free function, matching object()/view()'s own one-call convention
decision.chose: Keep the free function — ratifying the minion's own reading of my brief.
decision.why: The owner's own words here were exploratory, not a spec ("I don't know if it's class.icon... maybe it's class name dot inspect"), while object()/view() already establish the house convention this module uses (law 6, one of everything). A literal per-instance .inspect() would need a shared base class (this codebase has none) or a global Object.prototype patch — a much bigger, riskier change than the owner asked for. A class that wants the dot-call feel can opt in with one line (`MyClass.prototype.inspect = function(opts){ return inspect(this, opts); }`), the same opt-in shape `track()` already uses — not built now, just noted as the recipe if ever wanted.

Keep Part 1 scoped to one proof page, log the sitewide rollout as a named, deliberate follow-up
decision.chose: Keep Part 1 scoped as built — the proof on /framework/ux/Content/Object/ is enough to land Part 1.
decision.why: My own minion-part1/requirements.md explicitly scoped this to ONE page on purpose, to keep Part 1 landable by one Sonnet minion in one pass without touching a heavily-depended-on core file.
